'''Andrew Michael Harrison''' (born October 28, 1994) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Mitteldeutscher BC]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga]]. He was considered one of the top recruits for 2013.<ref>{{cite web|title=The Rivals150: 2013 Prospect Ranking|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/recruiting/rankings/rank-2752|access-date=October 5, 2012|work=Rivals.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Andrew Harrison Player Profiles – Scout.com|url=http://www.scout.com/player/4763121n-andrew-harrison|access-date=October 5, 2012|work=Scout.com}}</ref> He attended Travis High School in [[Richmond, Texas]], and played college basketball for the [[University of Kentucky]] along with his twin brother, [[Aaron Harrison]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Harrison twins choose Kentucky|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/8462850|last1=Rankin|first1=Reggie|last2=Telep|first2=Dave|access-date=May 20, 2023|work=ESPN.com|date=October 5, 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Raphielle|last=Johnson|title=2013 guards Aaron and Andrew Harrison verbally commit to attend Kentucky|url=http://collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2012/10/04/2013-guards-aaron-and-andrew-harrison-verbally-commit-to-attend-kentucky/|access-date=October 4, 2012|work=NBCSports.com|date=October 4, 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Larry |last=Vaught |title=Vaught's Views: Aaron Harrison shows he is a special player, like his twin brother |url=http://articles.centralkynews.com/2013-04-10/amnews/38442827_1_aaron-harrison-state-championship-travis-high-school |access-date=April 10, 2013 |work=CentralKYNews.com |date=April 10, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131112112414/http://articles.centralkynews.com/2013-04-10/amnews/38442827_1_aaron-harrison-state-championship-travis-high-school |archive-date=November 12, 2013 }}</ref>

==High school career==
[[File:20130403 MCDAAG Andrew Harrison.JPG|left|thumb|upright|Harrison in the [[2013 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]]]]
Harrison was widely regarded as a top-five player in the class of 2013 with [[Andrew Wiggins]], [[Jabari Parker]], [[Julius Randle]], and twin brother [[Aaron Harrison|Aaron]]. On March 9, 2013, Harrison helped the Fort Bend Travis Tigers defeat South Grand Prairie 46–38 to win the Class 5A state title in Texas. The Tigers finished #16 in the final ESPN 25 Power Rankings. Fort Bend Travis had lost in the Class 5A state title game the year before to Flower Mound Marcus.<ref>{{cite web|title=Texas final hoops rankings: FM Marcus, Kimball repeat as champs|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/high-school/texas/tag/_/name/fort-bend-travis/fort-bend-travis-tigers-defeated-by-flower-mound-marcus-the-year-before|last=Parker|first=Brandon|access-date=May 20, 2023|work=ESPN.com|date=March 13, 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=KEEP THE STATE TITLES COMING! CONGRATS TO THE FORT BEND TRAVIS TIGERS|url=http://www.krossover.com/blog/2013/03/keep-the-state-titles-coming-congrats-to-the-fort-bend-travis-tigers/|access-date=March 14, 2013|work=Krossover.com|date=March 14, 2013}}</ref>

Harrison played in both the [[Jordan Brand Classic#2013|2013 Jordan Brand Classic]] and the [[2013 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Steve |last=Jones |title=Andrew Harrison recaps McDonald's game |url=http://blogs.courier-journal.com/recruiting/2013/04/04/andrew-harrison-recaps-mcdonalds-game/ |access-date=April 4, 2013 |work=Courier-Journal.com |date=April 4, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130615063232/http://blogs.courier-journal.com/recruiting/2013/04/04/andrew-harrison-recaps-mcdonalds-game/ |archive-date=June 15, 2013 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Kentucky recruits dominate McDonald's All-American game rosters|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/ct-xpm-2013-03-31-ct-spt-0401-prep-bkb-mcdonalds-main-20130331-story.html|last=Kane|first=Colleen|access-date=March 31, 2013|work=ChicagoTribune.com|date=March 31, 2013}}</ref>

==College career==
In his two-year career at [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], Harrison averaged 10.1 points, 2.7 rebounds and 3.8 assists in 79 games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/andrew-harrison-1.html|title=Andrew Harrison Stats|work=Sports-Reference.com|access-date=October 31, 2015}}</ref> Harrison and his brother, Aaron, helped lead Kentucky to successive [[Final Fours]] in 2014 and 2015, but came up empty-handed both times after losing in the 2014 title game to [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|Connecticut]] and 2015 the semi-finals to [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin]].<ref name=chron>{{cite web|url=https://www.chron.com/sports/college/article/Reports-Aaron-and-Andrew-Harrison-leaving-6187065.php|title=Aaron and Andrew Harrison leaving Kentucky to enter NBA draft|work=Chron.com|date=April 9, 2015|access-date=April 9, 2015}}</ref>

On April 9, 2015, Harrison declared for the [[2015 NBA draft|NBA draft]], forgoing his final two years of college eligibility. He was joined alongside his twin brother Aaron and fellow Kentucky teammates [[Karl-Anthony Towns]], [[Willie Cauley-Stein]], [[Trey Lyles]], [[Devin Booker]], and [[Dakari Johnson]].<ref name="chron"/>

==Professional career==

===Iowa Energy (2015–2016)===
On June 25, 2015, Harrison was selected with the 44th overall pick by the [[Phoenix Suns]] in the [[2015 NBA draft]]. His rights were then traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in exchange for [[Jon Leuer]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-acquire-andrew-harrison-150625|title=Grizzlies acquire Draft Rights to Andrew Harrison from Suns|work=NBA.com|date=June 25, 2015|access-date=May 20, 2023}}</ref> He joined the Grizzlies for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]] and averaged 5.4 points, 2.0 rebounds and 3.0 assists in five games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/nba/teams/Memphis-Grizzlies/14/Rosters/Summer_League/2015|title=2015 Memphis Grizzlies Orlando Pro Summer League Roster|work=RealGM.com|access-date=December 1, 2016}}</ref> On October 31, 2015, he was acquired by the [[Iowa Energy]] of the [[NBA Development League]], the affiliate team of the Grizzlies.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/iowa-energy-announce-returning-affiliate-tryout-players-and-draft-rights-players-for-2015-training/n-5065432|title=Iowa Energy Announce Returning, Affiliate, Tryout Players and Draft Rights Players for 2015 Training|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 31, 2015|access-date=October 31, 2015}}</ref> He made his professional debut for the Energy on November 14 in a 98–95 win over the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]], recording 11 points and seven assists in 29 minutes.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20151114/IWASXF/|title=Skyforce Fall Against Energy 98–95 In Home Opener|work=NBA.com|date=November 14, 2015|access-date=January 31, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160219201750/http://dleague.nba.com/games/20151114/IWASXF/|archive-date=February 19, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> On February 16, 2016, he scored a season-high 36 points in a 115–105 loss to the [[Canton Charge]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FJPqyV_z3Gs|title=Andrew Harrison Drops Season-High 36 Points for Iowa Energy!|work=YouTube.com|date=February 16, 2016|access-date=July 10, 2016}}</ref> In 46 games for Iowa in 2015–16, he averaged 18.5 points, 4.3 rebounds, 4.9 assists and 1.5 steals per game.

===Memphis Grizzlies (2016–2018)===
After re-joining the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/summer-league-roster-160705|title=Grizzlies announce NBA Summer League 2016 roster|work=NBA.com|date=July 5, 2016|access-date=May 20, 2023}}</ref> Harrison signed a multi-year deal with the team on July 12, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/harrison-signed-160712|title=Grizzlies sign Andrew Harrison to multi-year contract|work=NBA.com|date=July 12, 2016|access-date=July 12, 2016}}</ref> On November 30, 2016, he scored a then career-high 21 points in a 120–105 loss to the [[Toronto Raptors]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899718|title=Lowry, DeRozan lift Raptors over Grizzlies 120–105|work=ESPN.com|date=November 30, 2016|access-date=December 1, 2016}}</ref> He made his debut in the [[2017 NBA playoffs|NBA playoffs]] on April 15, 2017, scoring 10 points in just under 20 minutes off the bench in a 111–82 loss to the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/harrian01/gamelog/2017/|title=Andrew Harrison 2016–17 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=July 19, 2017}}</ref>

On February 7, 2018, Harrison scored a career-high 23 points in a 92–88 loss to the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975554|title=Rubio, Hood lead Jazz over Grizzlies 92–88 for 7th straight|work=ESPN.com|date=February 7, 2018|access-date=February 7, 2018}}</ref> A week later, he set a new career high with 28 points in a 121–114 loss to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975607|title=George, Westbrook's triple-double lead OKC past Grizzlies|work=ESPN.com|date=February 14, 2018|access-date=February 14, 2018}}</ref> Harrison missed nine games in March 2018 due to a right wrist injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975799|title=Crabbe, LeVert lead Nets over Grizzlies 118–115|work=ESPN.com|date=March 19, 2018|access-date=March 19, 2018}}</ref>

On November 1, 2018, Harrison was waived by the Grizzlies.<ref>{{cite web|title=Memphis Grizzlies waive Andrew Harrison|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-waive-andrew-harrison-181101|date=November 1, 2018|website=NBA.com|access-date=November 1, 2018}}</ref>

===Cleveland Cavaliers (2018)===
On November 9, 2018, Harrison signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/harrison-signing-181109|title=Cavaliers Sign Andrew Harrison to Two-Way Contract|last=Adams|first=Nick|work=NBA.com|date=November 9, 2018|access-date=May 20, 2023}}</ref> He was waived by the Cavaliers on December 2, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/jones-blossomgame-signing-181202|title=Cavs Sign Jalen Jones and Jaron Blossomgame to Two-Way Contracts|last=Sykes|first=Joseph|work=NBA.com|date=December 2, 2018|access-date=May 20, 2023}}</ref>

===New Orleans Pelicans (2018–2019)===
On December 5, 2018, Harrison signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/pelicans-sign-andrew-harrison-two-way-contract|title=Pelicans sign Andrew Harrison to two-way contract|work=NBA.com|date=December 5, 2018|access-date=December 5, 2018}}</ref> He was waived by the Pelicans on January 8, 2019.<ref>{{cite news|title=Pelicans Waive Andrew Harrison|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/pelicans-waive-andrew-harrison-01-08-19|date=January 8, 2019|last=Gonzales|first=Caroline|website=NBA.com|access-date=May 20, 2023}}</ref>

===Khimki (2019)===
On February 27, 2019, Harrison signed with Russian club [[BC Khimki|Khimki]] for the rest of the 2018–19 season.<ref>{{cite web|title=ANDREW HARRISON JOINED KHIMKI MOSCOW REGION|url=https://en.bckhimki.ru/news/clubnews/2019/february/1400/|date=February 27, 2019|website=bckhimki.ru|access-date=February 27, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Khimki revamps backcourt with Harrison|url=https://www.euroleague.net/news/i/9hrsqaiokafrhq9e/khimki-revamps-backcourt-with-harrison|date=February 27, 2019|website=euroleague.net|access-date=February 27, 2019}}</ref>

===Santa Cruz Warriors (2019–2020)===
On September 5, 2019, Harrison signed with the [[Golden State Warriors]]. On October 19, 2019, the Warriors released Harrison.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/andrew-harrison-waived-by-warriors/|title = Andrew Harrison: Waived by Warriors| date=October 19, 2019 }}</ref> He ultimately landed on the roster of the Warriors' [[G League]] affiliate, the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Santa Cruz Warriors Announce 2019–20 Opening Night Roster |url=https://santacruz.gleague.nba.com/news/santa-cruz-warriors-announce-2019-20-opening-night-roster/ |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 9, 2019 |date=November 7, 2019 |archive-date=February 5, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210205101021/https://santacruz.gleague.nba.com/news/santa-cruz-warriors-announce-2019-20-opening-night-roster/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> He averaged 15.5 points, 5.1 assists, 3.8 rebounds and 1.2 steals per game.<ref>{{cite news |last=Varney |first=Dennis |title=Catch up with 36 ex-Cats playing pro basketball in leagues outside the NBA |url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/ex-cats/article241420196.html |access-date=May 16, 2020 |work=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]] |date=March 26, 2020}}</ref>

===Beijing Royal Fighters (2020–2021)===
After his stint with the Santa Cruz Warriors, Harrison signed with the Chinese team [[Beijing Royal Fighters]]. In his first game, he recorded 11 points and 5 rebounds in a winning effort against the [[Qingdao Eagles]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/China/2020/1202_15106_7300.asp|title=Beijing Royal Fighters – Qingdao Eagles 105–92|publisher=EuroBasket|date=December 2, 2020|access-date=January 1, 2021}}</ref>

===Windy City Bulls (2022)===
On January 10, 2022, Harrison was traded from the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] to the [[Windy City Bulls]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021–22 NBA G League transactions|date=January 10, 2022|access-date=January 10, 2022}}</ref> However, he was waived on February 10 after a season-ending injury.<ref>{{cite web|title=2021–2022 Windy City Bulls Transactions History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/dleague/teams/Windy-City-Bulls/44/Transaction_History/2022|website=RealGM.com|access-date=March 29, 2022}}</ref>

===Merkezefendi Belediyesi Denizli Basket (2022–2023)===
On July 31, 2022, he signed with [[Merkezefendi Belediyesi Denizli Basket|Merkezefendi Bld. Denizli Basket]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi|Turkish Basketball Super League]] (BSL).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/tr/tbl-tr/1373920/yukatel-merkezefendi-belediyesi-andrew-harrison-transferini-resmen-acikladi/|title=Yukatel Merkezefendi Belediyesi, Andrew Harrison Transferini Resmen Açıkladı|date=July 31, 2022|website=|publisher=Eurohoops|language=tr|access-date=August 5, 2022}}</ref>

===PAOK Thessaloniki (2023–2024)===
On July 30, 2023, Harrison signed with Greek club [[P.A.O.K. BC|PAOK Thessaloniki]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/paok-inks-andrew-harrison/|title=PAOK inks Andrew Harrison|last=|first=|date=July 30, 2023|website=|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=July 30, 2023 |last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }}</ref> On February 6, 2024, he mutually parted ways with the team.

===Yalovaspor (2024)===
On February 6, 2024, he signed with [[Yalovaspor BK|Yalovaspor]] of the [[Türkiye Basketbol Ligi]] (TBL).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Turkey/news/852268/Yalovaspor-tabs-Andrew-Harrison-ex-PAOK|title=Yalovaspor tabs Andrew Harrison, ex PAOK|last=|first=|date=February 6, 2024|website=|publisher=Eurobasket|language=En|access-date=February 2, 2026}}</ref>

===Mitteldeutscher BC (2026–present)===
On January 19, 2026, he signed with [[Mitteldeutscher BC]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga]] (BBL).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://syntainics-mbc.de/andrew-harrison-kommt-stephon-jelks-geht/|title=Andrew Harrison kommt, Stephon Jelks geht|last=|first=|date=January 19, 2026|website=syntainics-mbc.de|publisher=|language=de|access-date=February 2, 2026}}</ref>
